data.text:
## file-manager — File manager (pattern, archetype browse-collections)
Browse, organize, preview and act on files and folders arranged in a hierarchy of locations.
Aliases: file browser, Finder, Explorer, drive
Anatomy: Locations (Sidebar of places and favourites); Path (Where you are); Item area (Files and folders here); Preview (A look at the selected file); Toolbar (View and file operations)
Related — uses: tree-view, breadcrumbs, split-pane, tabs, menu, drag-reorder | specializes: overview-detail | neighbors: data-table
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Item view [layout] — How are files shown, and where does a preview appear?
  - view (single-select: one id) — Item view
      icons: Icons (e.g. Finder icon view)
      list: List (e.g. Finder list view)
      columns: Columns — Miller columns, one per level (e.g. Finder column view)
      gallery: Gallery — Large preview with a filmstrip (e.g. Finder gallery view)
      details-table: Details table (e.g. Windows Explorer details)
  - preview (single-select: one id) — Preview placement
      none: None (e.g. Terminal file lists)
      preview-pane: Preview pane — Beside the item area (e.g. Windows Explorer preview pane)
      overlay-preview: Overlay preview — A transient full preview (e.g. macOS Quick Look)
      viewer-page: Viewer page — Opens a viewer over the drive (e.g. Google Drive preview)
* Navigation structure [composition] — How are locations traversed, and how many are open at once?
  - traversal (single-select: one id) — Traversal
      tree-plus-content: Tree plus content (e.g. Windows Explorer)
      miller-columns: Miller columns (e.g. Finder column view)
      drill-down-with-breadcrumbs: Drill-down with breadcrumbs (e.g. Google Drive)
      search-first: Search first — Recents and search over folders (e.g. Dropbox home)
  - multi (single-select: one id) — Multiple locations
      single-window: Single window (e.g. Mobile file apps)
      tabs: Tabs (e.g. Finder tabs, Windows 11 Explorer tabs)
      dual-pane: Dual pane — Two locations side by side (e.g. Total Commander)
* Metadata [content] — What does each file show about itself?
  - metadata (multi-select: list of ids) — Metadata shown
      name: Name (e.g. All)
      size-and-kind: Size and kind (e.g. Finder list view)
      dates: Dates (e.g. Finder list view)
      tags-and-colours: Tags and colours (e.g. Finder tags)
      owner-and-sharing: Owner and sharing (e.g. Google Drive)
      thumbnails: Thumbnails (e.g. Windows large icons)
      last-change: Last change — The last commit or change message shown per file or folder (e.g. GitHub — Repository file tree)
* Grouping [scope] — Are files grouped, and can a folder be a query?
  - grouping (single-select: one id) — Grouping
      none: None (e.g. Default views)
      by-kind: By kind (e.g. Finder Use Groups)
      by-date: By date (e.g. Finder Use Groups)
      saved-searches-as-folders: Saved searches as folders (e.g. macOS Smart Folders)
* Shared ownership [collaboration] — How are other people’s files and activity shown?
  - ownership (multi-select: list of ids) — Ownership surfaces
      local-only: Local only (e.g. Finder on a local disk)
      shared-with-me-area: Shared-with-me area (e.g. Google Drive)
      activity-panel: Activity panel — Who changed what (e.g. Google Drive activity)

## data-table — Data table (pattern, archetype browse-collections)
Items as rows against attributes as columns, built for scanning, comparing, sorting, filtering and acting on many items at once.
Aliases: data grid, table view, details view
Anatomy: Header (Column names and their controls); Row (One item); Cell (One attribute value); Toolbar (Collection operations); Footer (Aggregates and paging)
Related — uses: sort-control, filter-controls, bulk-actions, pagination, inline-edit, drawer | specializes: overview-detail | neighbors: spreadsheet, comparison-table, pivot-table

## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      flat: Flat (e.g. Overflow menus)
      sections: Sections (e.g. Google Docs menus)
      cascading-submenus: Cascading submenus (e.g. Desktop menu bars)
      mega-menu: Mega menu — Multi-column panel (e.g. Retail department menus)
* Item content [content] — What does each item show?
  - item (multi-select: list of ids) — Item content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Google Docs)
      shortcut-hint: Shortcut hint (e.g. macOS menus)
      checkmark-state: Checkmark state (e.g. View menus)
      description: Description (e.g. GitHub menus)
* Item set [initiative] — Who decides which items appear and in what order?
  - itemSet (single-select: one id) — Item set
      fixed: Fixed (e.g. Most menus)
      depends-on-selection: Depends on selection (e.g. Context menus)
      adaptive: Adaptive — The system reorders by use (e.g. Office 2000 personalized menus)
      adaptable: Adaptable — The person reorders (e.g. Office Quick Access Toolbar)
* Form [layout] — What shape is it?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      vertical-list: Vertical list (e.g. Most menus)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Blender pie menus)
      icon-grid: Icon grid (e.g. Google apps launcher)
      horizontal-bar: Horizontal bar (e.g. Toolbars)

## chart — Chart (pattern, archetype analyze)
A visual encoding of data values as marks and channels so a person can see distributions, comparisons and trends.
Aliases: plot, graph, visualization
Anatomy: Marks (The visual elements); Axes and scales (How values map to space); Legend (How channels are decoded); Tooltip (Detail on demand for a mark); Controls (Encoding and filter affordances)
Related — uses: tooltip, filter-controls, stat-tile | specializes: analyze | neighbors: coordinated-views, pivot-table, dashboard
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Mark encoding [encoding] — What marks and channels carry the data?
  - markType (single-select: one id) — Mark type
      points: Points (e.g. Scatterplots)
      bars: Bars (e.g. Bar charts)
      lines: Lines (e.g. Line charts)
      areas: Areas (e.g. Area charts)
      arcs: Arcs (e.g. Pie and donut)
      cells: Cells (e.g. Heatmaps)
      glyphs: Glyphs (e.g. Radar and parallel coordinates)
  - channels (multi-select: list of ids) — Channels used
      position: Position (e.g. Cartesian plots)
      length: Length (e.g. Bars)
      colour-hue-or-value: Colour hue or value (e.g. Choropleths)
      size: Size (e.g. Bubble charts)
      shape: Shape (e.g. Categorical scatters)
      opacity: Opacity (e.g. Overplotting control)
      animation: Animation — A variable — almost always time — is mapped to motion over frames rather than to a static visual channel, with a play control and a scrubber; bar chart races, animated scatter trails (e.g. Flourish — Bar chart race)
* Scale and axes [layout] — How is the value space laid out?
  - scale (single-select: one id) — Scale
      linear: Linear (e.g. Most charts)
      logarithmic: Logarithmic (e.g. Finance log scales)
      ordinal-or-band: Ordinal or band (e.g. Category axes)
      time: Time (e.g. Time-seri

data.text:
## command-palette — Command palette (pattern, archetype navigate)
A keyboard-summoned search box that finds and runs commands, jumps to places and objects, and teaches shortcuts along the way.
Aliases: command bar, quick open, launcher, Cmd+K menu
Anatomy: Trigger (The shortcut or button that summons it); Query (The typed text); Results (Ranked commands, places and objects); Arguments (Follow-up inputs a command needs)
Related — uses: autocomplete, modal-dialog, menu | specializes: navigate | neighbors: search-results, menu
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Results [content] — What can be found, and what does each result show?
  - types (multi-select: list of ids) — Result types
      commands: Commands (e.g. VS Code Command Palette)
      places: Places (e.g. Linear go-to)
      objects-and-files: Objects and files (e.g. VS Code Quick Open)
      settings-toggles: Settings toggles (e.g. Chrome omnibox actions)
      system-and-web-results: System and web results (e.g. Spotlight, Raycast)
      ai-answers: AI answers (e.g. Raycast AI)
      people: People — Finding and jumping to a specific person, distinct from a command, a place, a file, a settings toggle, a system/web result, or an AI answer. (e.g. Notion — Search and actions)
      code-symbols: Code symbols — Classes, symbols and other code-structure results, distinct from commands, places, files, settings, web/system results or AI answers — the same gap found in the autocomplete entry's IntelliSense instance. (e.g. IntelliJ IDEA — Search Everywhere)
  - detail (single-select: one id) — Result detail
      name-only: Name only (e.g. Minimal palettes)
      name-and-shortcut: Name and shortcut (e.g. VS Code keybinding hints)
      name-and-description: Name and description (e.g. Linear)
      preview-pane: Preview pane (e.g. Raycast detail view)
* Summoning [invocation] — How is the palette opened and moded?
  - summon (multi-select: list of ids) — Summon by
      in-app-shortcut: In-app shortcut (e.g. Cmd+K in Linear)
      system-wide-hotkey: System-wide hotkey (e.g. Spotlight, Raycast, Alfred)
      visible-search-button: Visible search button (e.g. GitHub command palette button)
      prefix-characters: Prefix characters — Typed prefixes switch modes (e.g. VS Code > and @)
* Arguments [flow] — How does a command collect what it needs?
  - arguments (single-select: one id) — Argument collection
      runs-immediately: Runs immediately (e.g. Toggle sidebar)
      nested-pages: Nested pages (e.g. Linear Change status submenu)
      inline-argument-fields: Inline argument fields (e.g. Raycast arguments)
      conversational-follow-up: Conversational follow-up (e.g. AI command bars)
* Ranking [initiative] — Who decides which results come first?
  - ranking (single-select: one id) — Ranking
      fuzzy-match: Fuzzy match (e.g. VS Code)
      frequency-and-recency: Frequency and recency (e.g. VS Code recently used)
      context-of-the-selection: Context of the selection (e.g. Linear commands for the selected issue)
      predicted-next-action: Predicted next action (e.g. Research prototypes)
      pinned-by-the-person: Pinned by the person — The person fixes chosen commands to the top of the list; the order is authored rather than matched, learned or contextual (e.g. Obsidian — Command palette)
      manually-pinned: Manually pinned — The person manually pins specific commands to the top of the list, rather than the system ranking by fuzzy match, frequency/recency, selection context or predicted next action. (e.g. Obsidian — Command palette)
* Command scope [scope] — How far does it reach?
  - scope (single-select: one id) — Scope
      current-app: Current app (e.g. Figma Quick actions)
      current-selection: Current selection (e.g. Linear)
      operating-system: Operating system (e.g. Spotlight)
      connected-apps: Connected apps (e.g. Raycast extensions)
* Placement [layout] — Where does it appear?
  - placement (single-select: one id)
